answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through proof of burn. To register, entities must destroy native tokens at an unspendable burn address. This forces an attacker to incur the verifiable cost of permanently liquidated capital per identity, stopping fake swarms from eroding trust like sinkholes in karst terrain. Even a lightweight sparrow client must burn assets alongside hardy juniper nodes. However, capital-rich adversaries can absorb heavy burn costs, marginalizing underfunded agents.
